overview: A Pacific Northwest storm system brings snow to the Utah, Wyoming and Montana mountains through Saturday, then a weaker system follows around Monday. The Central Rockies get showers through Saturday and more fast-moving storms are possible through Thanksgiving week.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A storm from the Pacific Northwest passes over Utah through early Saturday, with snow focused increasingly on northern Utah. Powder Mountain leads with 10 inches, most of it on Friday. The NWS is calling for more, 12 to 20 inches Friday through Monday, and a Winter Storm Warning runs from Thursday night to Saturday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A system brings snow to the western slopes and passes Friday, with the Tetons under a Winter Weather Advisory. Grand Targhee leads with 10 inches, 6 of them on Friday. Winds ease and more snow showers follow into Monday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Moisture from a storm moving across the Intermountain West brings snow to the mountains through Saturday. Telluride and Crested Butte both expect about 7 inches. Some gusts could make travel harder, and a brief snow squall is possible near Interstate 70 Friday morning.

ahead.text: The Climate Prediction Center expects a weaker, more progressive system to move through the West around Wednesday Nov 25 into the following days. It has less confidence in the details.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
